clue.text: Devastated as rich mother makes personal appeal

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wealthy matriarch, ruined, still wins people over through sheer force of personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is the compelling charm of an individual, a synonym for the magnetism that draws others to them.

clue.text: Restrain, for the most part, surly mongrel dog

parts.note: to curb is to hold back or restrain

explanation.surface: Keep a bad-tempered stray on a tight leash, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a worthless or aggressive mixed-breed dog, so the long phrase is a dictionary gloss.

clue.text: For instance, country in ancient kingdom

the Middle Eastern country

explanation.surface: Reads like a quiz prompt asking for an example of a country located inside some old realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Assyria was a Mesopotamian empire of antiquity, centred on the upper Tigris.

clue.text: Seaweed girl and husband found by bog

parts.note: a girl's name
H is the standard abbreviation for husband
a moss is a peat bog, especially in Scotland and northern England

explanation.surface: A woman and her husband stumble upon seaweed beside a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish moss, or carrageen, is an edible red alga gathered on Atlantic shores.

clue.text: Bird that might give ram/ewes anthrax

indicators.note: what the letters might give is something they could be made into once rearranged

parts.note: all fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A worry that some bird could pass a deadly disease to sheep of either sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash just joins two words of fodder; the sheep and the disease are pure scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx shearwater is a seabird that skims low over the waves, named after the Isle of Man.

clue.text: A place attended by unruly mob — coolness is required

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: When a rowdy crowd turns up at a venue, someone has to keep a cool head.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb means self-possession under pressure, so it is a synonym for composure or coolness.

clue.text: US president has a dance

parts.note: James K. Polk, 11th president of the United States
taken as written

explanation.surface: The American head of state takes a turn on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance in duple time.

clue.text: Old special train driver, inexperienced on the road, is being tested

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

indicators.note: a special version is made differently from the usual, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a learner driver displays an L plate in Britain

explanation.surface: A novice driving an old special train is under assessment.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers must show a red L plate, so a driver new to the road is L.

clue.text: Awful noise abuser in capital

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful noise-maker is causing trouble in some big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Buenos Aires is the capital city of Argentina.

clue.text: Modern laywomen going off into the past?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a looser, descriptive definition of a phrase used with 'a trip'

indicators.note: things going off are spoiling or exploding, so the letters break apart and reform

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Contemporary non-clerical women heading off into history.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that 'Modern' supplies the letters of a journey backwards in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip down memory lane is a nostalgic journey back through one's own recollections of earlier times.

clue.text: Act of bravado involving a single slug?

definitions.text: Act of bravado involving a single slug?

parts.words: Act of bravado involving a single slug?
parts.note: surface reading: a daredevil stunt with one garden slug, or a single gulp of spirits
setter's reading: a slug is slang for a bullet, and the deadly game loads one round into a revolver

explanation.walkthrough: A slug may be a mollusc or a slug of whisky; here it is a bullet, one chamber of six loaded.
explanation.definitionFit: The game is a show of reckless daring in which a player spins a revolver's cylinder holding one cartridge and pulls the trigger.

clue.text: Deliberately set fire to church by rocky peak

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Arson at a chapel that stands beside a crag.
explanation.definitionFit: To torch something is informal for burning it on purpose, typically in arson.

clue.text: Thai so tasty — specially cooked, in other words

indicators.note: food specially cooked has been prepared and transformed, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A restaurant review: the Thai food was delicious because it was prepared with care.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a restatement or clarification of what has just been said.

clue.text: Republic created by Romanians following revolution

indicators.note: after a revolution things are turned upside down, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A state founded by the people of Romania after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Romania did become a republic after its 1989 revolution, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: San Marino is a tiny republic enclosed by Italy, claimed as the world's oldest.

clue.text: Sailor only gets one shellfish

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
a means one
lone means sole or only

explanation.surface: A seaman is allowed just a single shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter for 'one' goes in front of the word for 'only' once the sailor has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible sea snail with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Noble Italian family associated with very laid back girl loved by Pip

parts.note: the House of Este ruled Ferrara and Modena

indicators.note: laid back, read literally, means put down backwards, so the word is written right to left

parts.note: all can mean very or entirely, as in 'all alone'

explanation.surface: An aristocratic Italian house linked to a very relaxed young woman whom Pip adores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' poses as 'relaxed' but signals a reversal. Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Estella is the cold, beautiful ward of Miss Havisham, the object of Pip's devotion in the novel.

clue.text: Conman, rotten critter going round Kansas

indicators.note: one set of letters going round another encircles it, holding it within
something rotten has gone bad and fallen apart, so its letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
KS is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Kansas

explanation.surface: A swindler, a nasty creature, travelling through the Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickster is someone who deceives or swindles people, much as a confidence man does.

clue.text: Terribly ironic about son cutting tooth

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other
something done terribly is botched, so the letters end up out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: How sadly ironic that a boy should be teething.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting tooth' suggests a baby teething but is the definition: a tooth for cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisors are the sharp front teeth used for biting and slicing food.

clue.text: Two coppers with fish, head cut off — baked item

indicators.note: beheading something removes its top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and a PC, police constable, is a copper
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A pair of police officers with a decapitated fish, served as a bake.
explanation.walkthrough: The two coppers are different: one is the metal's symbol, the other a British policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupcake is a small sponge cake baked in a paper case, so it is one baked thing.

clue.text: Famous actor, one appearing in musical!

I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A celebrated actor takes a part in a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark nods to the title Oliver!, which carries one.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was one of the great English stage and screen actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: I may, concealing German statues etc.

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written
GER is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A tentative admission of hiding a German, followed by a list of sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery means visual images collectively, such as statues and other representations in art.

clue.text: A tripper crashed heading for yonder county

indicators.note: something crashed is smashed up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its start, so only its opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A day-tripper has an accident on the way to a distant county.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the song 'It's a Long Way to Tipperary', which supplies 'yonder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is a county in the Irish province of Munster.

clue.text: Affair in flat with leader of Tories

parts.note: even means level or flat

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so just the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A political scandal conducted in an apartment with the head of the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' and 'flat' paint a liaison in an apartment; flat here means level. Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occurrence or happening, one sense of affair, as in 'a grand affair'.

clue.text: Poet in Pembroke, at shop

indicators.note: in signals that the word sits inside the following run of letters

parts.note: letters running across the end of one word and into the next two

explanation.surface: A poet spotted in a shop in the Welsh town of Pembroke.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, author of the great odes.

clue.text: Declaration about split in government agency

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: a statement is a formal declaration
split is slang for leave

explanation.surface: An announcement concerning a rift inside an official body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' looks like a noun for a rift but is the verb meaning to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The State Department is the US federal ministry responsible for foreign affairs.

clue.text: Chess champion held by Italian

indicators.note: something held by a word is inside it, so the letters sit within it

parts.note: letters in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A chess title-holder captured by an opponent from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Mikhail Tal, the Latvian 'Magician from Riga', was world champion in 1960-61.
explanation.definitionFit: Tal held the world chess championship title, so he is a famous chess champion.

clue.text: French girl requires doctor, we hear, after onset of yaws

parts.note: the first letter of the word

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
